subject.title: fix(slack): warn on disabled channel drops

question: Should this Slack-specific fix close the broader denial-observability issue, or should the remaining channel implementations stay canonically tracked?
rationale: The code fix is bounded and technically sound, but the linked issue describes provider-agnostic observability and names non-Slack channels, so issue completion depends on maintainer scope intent.

options.title: Land Slack, retain broader tracking
options.body: Merge this PR as the Slack implementation and keep or narrow the linked issue for other channel plugins that still drop explicit denials silently.

options.title: Treat the issue as Slack-only
options.body: Merge this PR with the closing reference and explicitly record that other channel behavior is outside the issue's accepted scope.

options.title: Broaden before merge
options.body: Hold this PR until equivalent owner-plugin warnings and proof are added for every channel considered part of the issue.

recommendation.title: Land Slack, retain broader tracking
recommendation.body: Merge this PR as the Slack implementation and keep or narrow the linked issue for other channel plugins that still drop explicit denials silently.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch author also owns the proposed Slack behavior, tests, and live-QA scenario and is best positioned to clarify the intended issue scope.
